data.reference_solution:
def kthSmallest(root: Optional[TreeNode], k: int) -> int:
    values = []
    def traverse(node):
        if not node:
            return
        values.append(node.val)
        traverse(node.left)
        traverse(node.right)
    traverse(root)
    values.sort()
    return values[k - 1]

events.label: Solver: design the algorithm
events.detail: Iterative Inorder Traversal · claims O(H + k) time

data.key_insight: An inorder traversal of a Binary Search Tree (BST) visits the nodes in ascending order of their values. By performing an iterative inorder traversal using a stack, we can stop exactly at the k-th visited node, giving an optimal solution.

steps.title: Initialize Stack and Current Pointer
steps.detail: Create an empty stack to keep track of nodes and set a pointer current to the root of the BST.

steps.title: Traverse Left Subtree
steps.detail: Iteratively push all left children onto the stack until we reach the leftmost node (the smallest element).

steps.title: Process Node and Decrement k
steps.detail: Pop a node from the stack, decrement k, and check if k is 0. If it is, this node's value is our answer.

steps.title: Move to Right Subtree
steps.detail: If k is not 0, move the current pointer to the right child of the popped node and repeat the process.

data.pattern_summary: Visiting nodes in a specific structured order (left, root, right) to leverage the inherent sorting property of a Binary Search Tree.

pattern_options.name: Iterative Inorder Traversal
pattern_options.feedback: This fits because walking the BST in ascending order allows you to stop right at the k-th element.

pattern_options.name: Hash map lookup
pattern_options.feedback: A hash map doesn't help track hierarchical tree paths or sorted order without visiting everything anyway.

pattern_options.name: Two pointers
pattern_options.feedback: Two pointers work best on linear sequences like arrays or strings, not tree structures.

pattern_options.name: Breadth-First Search
pattern_options.feedback: BFS visits nodes level by level, which does not naturally yield sorted values for a BST.

signals.hint: Implies a specific sorted structure where left children are smaller and right children are larger than the parent.
Indicates you are looking for a specific rank in sorted order rather than searching for a specific value.

data.brute_force_idea: Collect every single node value from the tree into a list, sort the entire list, and return the element at index k minus one.
data.brute_force_why: Traversing all n nodes takes O(n) time, and sorting the resulting list of n elements takes O(n log n) time.
data.bottleneck: Sorting all collected values is wasteful because the tree structure already guarantees a semi-sorted order if traversed correctly.
bottleneck_hints: Look at how the values are collected and processed after the traversal finishes.
Ask yourself if you actually need to look at every single node and then sort them all from scratch.
Consider whether you can process the nodes in the correct order during traversal instead of sorting afterward.

        traverse(node.right)
    traverse(root)
    values.sort()
    return values[k - 1]

data.overview: The kthSmallest algorithm finds the kth smallest value in a BST by performing an iterative inorder traversal. Because a BST's inorder traversal visits nodes in sorted order, we simply decrement k as we visit each node until k reaches zero.
data.intuition: Imagine exploring a building where rooms are numbered in sorted order. You always dive as far left as possible into the smallest available room first, then visit the room, and then check its right hallway.

data.insight: The brute force solution collects all node values into a list and sorts them, wasting time on nodes larger than the kth element. The optimized iterative inorder traversal visits nodes in ascending order and stops immediately when it reaches the kth element. This avoids processing the entire tree when k is small.

derivation.note: The outer loop runs at most n times across the traversal.
The inner loop goes down the left branch proportional to tree height h.
Pops execute exactly k times before returning the answer.

data.time_summary: Lines 7-9 descend to the leftmost node taking O(h) time, and lines 11-16 process each node in sorted order up to k. Summing these operations yields O(h + k) time in the worst case, aligning with the measured evidence where steps scale linearly with n.
data.space_summary: The stack holds at most h nodes at any time during the descent, where h is the height of the tree. Therefore, the space complexity is O(h).
data.takeaway: When searching for the kth element in a sorted structure like a BST, use controlled in-order traversal with an early exit instead of full collection and sorting.
mistakes: Forgetting that k is 1-indexed and miscalculating the decrement condition.
Traversing the entire tree when k is small instead of terminating early at k == 0.
Confusing tree height h with total nodes n when analyzing the space complexity of the recursion stack.
